source_refs.note: 1- Gonads (Testes): a main subheading of 17.1.1 Male Reproductive System, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 73-74.

blocks.text: Two testes are located outside the abdomen in a skin pouch called scrotum. Each testis is oval-shaped and measures about 3–5 cm in length and 2–3 cm in width. A testis is composed of highly convoluted seminiferous tubules. The wall of the seminiferous tubules i.e., germinal epithelium contains two types of cells i.e., germline cells and Sertoli cells. The germinal cells make sperms (spermatozoa) by meiosis. Sertoli cell nourish the developing sperms.

blocks.alt: Side by side. (a) Side view of the male pelvis: urinary bladder, rectum behind, pubic bone in front; prostate gland below the bladder; seminal vesicle behind it; the vas deferens rises from the epididymis and testis in the scrotum, passes over the bladder and joins the seminal vesicle duct as the ejaculatory duct; bulbourethral gland; urethra through the penis. (b) Right: a testis cut open: lobules of seminiferous tubules, rete testis, epididymis and vas deferens.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.1: (a) Male reproductive system; (b) Cross section of a testis (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.1).

The Vas deferens and Epididymis label lines run on to the same parts in (b), and a purple arrow leads from the Testis label to (b). (b) labels: Rete testis, Seminiferous tubules.
